analysis.title: US: September Employment Preview
key_insights: Nomura expects September nonfarm payrolls of +130k (consensus +104k), after +162k in August. Private payrolls are forecast at +120k (consensus +90k).
Nomura expects the unemployment rate to tick down to 4.0% from 4.1% in August (consensus 4.2%), the lowest since January 2025. Risks are skewed to the upside, meaning an unchanged 4.1% reading.

The below-consensus unemployment forecast rests on improving fundamentals plus September seasonality. Since 2010 the rate has surprised consensus to the downside by about 12bp on average in September, and came in below expectations in 11 of the past 16 years.
Nomura attributes the September seasonal pattern to a pickup in transitions from unemployment to nonparticipation after subdued summer readings, linked to the start of the school year.
Nomura expects modest positive revisions to August payrolls, consistent with the historical seasonal pattern of the second estimate versus the first.

Lead indicators for job gains are consistently positive. Weekly ADP employment continues to strengthen, and the four-week average of continuing claims through the September reference period fell to its lowest since June 2023.
Survey employment indices in several surveys are at multiyear highs. The September S&P PMI noted stronger activity and rising order backlogs encouraging firms to add headcount.

Government payrolls are forecast at +10k in September after +35k in August. Local government employment is expected to keep normalizing after sharp swings in education employment, and state government payrolls also rose.

Average hourly earnings are forecast at +0.2% m/m (consensus 0.3%), partly due to a negative calendar effect since the 12th of the month fell on a Saturday. Lead indicators point to gradual wage cooling.
The average workweek is forecast unchanged at 34.4 hours (consensus 34.3). Surveys point to a pickup, while Labor Day falling in the reference week may have weighed on hours.
TPS expirations remain a headwind to employment growth, likely smaller than in prior months. The 27 July expiration for about 350k Haitians likely weighed on education and health services employment.

El Salvador's TPS stayed in place beyond the scheduled 9 September, so Nomura does not expect a significant drag in September. Salvadoran-born workers are concentrated in construction, where strong hiring including data-center construction could offset any loss.

Layoff measures continue to trend lower. Initial claims have declined and the JOLTS layoff rate is subdued. Job-finding improved in August household-survey flows and U-6 fell to its lowest since June 2025.
Nomura expects the unemployment rate to keep declining gradually, reaching 3.9% by year-end 2027.
Policy implication: a report like this should strengthen the Fed's view that the labor market is steady and near full employment, keeping the Fed focused on inflation.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above-consensus payroll forecast points to a solid, broad-based labor market.
Below-consensus forecast, with risk that the rate stays unchanged at 4.1%.
Slower wage growth, partly a calendar effect, which supports a cooling wage narrative.
Prior month's first-estimate gain, expected to be revised up modestly.
Baseline for the expected September decline.

risk_factors: Unemployment rate may come in unchanged at 4.1% rather than the 4.0% forecast.
TPS expirations, especially Haiti's, reduce labor supply and weigh on education and health services employment.
Labor Day falling in the payroll reference week may have weighed on hours worked, though BLS calendar adjustment partly accounts for it.
Uncertainty ahead of the El Salvador TPS deadline may have led firms and workers to frontload some adjustment.

tension_points.bull_case: Nomura expects the rate to fall to 4.0% on lower layoffs, improving job finding and a September seasonal tendency to surprise below consensus.
tension_points.bear_case: Risks are skewed to the upside, meaning the rate could be unchanged at 4.1%, and TPS expirations are a near-term headwind to employment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An unchanged 4.1% unemployment reading in the September report.
